title: Derivative and Tangent of a Quadratic at a Point
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Use the limit definition of the derivative to find f'(2) for f(x) = x^2 - 4x + 1, and write the equation of the tangent line at x = 2.

steps.title: Evaluate f(2) and Form Difference Quotient
steps.explanation: Evaluate the function at the target point.
steps.why: Function value provides the y-coordinate of the point of tangency.

steps.title: Expand f(2 + h)
steps.why: Evaluation of the perturbed function coordinate.

steps.title: Compute Limit as h -> 0
steps.explanation: Cancel the constant terms and factor out h.
steps.why: Canceling h resolves the 0/0 indeterminate difference quotient.

steps.title: Construct Tangent Line Equation
steps.explanation: Substitute point (2, -3) and horizontal slope m = 0 into point-slope form.
steps.why: A derivative of zero produces a horizontal tangent line.
